Support RFP development, vendor evaluation, bid review, and systems integrator selection.
Establish controls network standards related to redundancy, segmentation, cybersecurity, and IT/OT integration.
Partner with commissioning teams to ensure systems are designed and implemented for successful functional performance testing.
Develop strategies for automation, remote monitoring, alarm management, DCIM integration, analytics, and digital-twin capabilities.
Manage and develop relationships with controls vendors, consultants, integrators, engineering partners, and internal stakeholders.
Help build and mentor an internal controls engineering organization as the business continues to scale.

Qualifications

10+ years of progressive controls, automation, instrumentation, or building systems engineering experience.
Significant experience supporting data centers, mission-critical facilities, hyperscale environments, colocation facilities, or other complex critical infrastructure.
Strong experience with BMS and/or EPMS architecture and implementation.
Experience serving as a technical owner, discipline lead, engineering lead, or senior technical authority on large capital projects.
Hands-on understanding of controls programming, system integration, troubleshooting, and field implementation.
Strong knowledge of building automation, mechanical controls, electrical monitoring, metering, alarms, and system communications.
Experience working with controls systems integrators and external engineering partners.
Familiarity with SCADA and DCIM integration.
Knowledge of controls protocols such as BACnet, Modbus, OPC UA, SNMP, and IEC 61850.

Ability to communicate complex technical concepts to engineers, contractors, vendors, executives, and other stakeholders.

jobs.title: Director of Engineering, Digital Experience
jobs.description:
Job Description

About the Role

Our Digital Experience engineering organization is growing from 16 to more than 21 engineers across multiple squads — including three squads working in a shared codebase — while delivering the most consequential initiatives on our roadmap. We're looking for a Director of Engineering to lead this organization through its next stage of growth: its strategy, its processes, its people, and its partnership with Product.
You'll lead through a layer of squad leads who own the day-to-day and performance of their squads (engineers and QA). Your job is to manage, coach, and develop those leads, inspect team-level outcomes, and own the health of the engineering organization as a whole.
The measure of this role is not individual output. It is whether the teams around you deliver faster, more predictably, and with fewer things in their way.
What You'll Own

Engineering Strategy
Be the engineering voice in strategic conversations about what we build and how we build it — participating from the first conversation on new initiatives, not after decisions are made.
Shape how the engineering organization is structured — squad composition, roles, and skill mix — to meet current-year objectives while planning for a multi-year horizon.
Own the point of view on our tech stack and architecture direction: whether what we have today supports where the product is going, and what needs to change before it becomes a constraint.
Partner with Product leadership as a peer when planning future years — Product brings the business perspective, you bring the engineering perspective, and together you organize the squads and the plans.

Engineering Leadership — Process and Tone
Set the process and tone for how engineering runs — the "how" (development and release processes) and the "what" (team functions and responsibilities) — without removing squad independence.
Establish and steward a release process appropriate for an organization of this size: who does what and why, checklists, rollback plans, and cross-team notification.
Define the development process end to end: how PRs move through the system, what the delivery pipeline looks like, how AI is incorporated into engineering work, and what happens when problems arise.
Be the leader engineers look to for expectations. When something isn't clear, work with the leads to make it clear.
Provide stewardship for the squads sharing a codebase as the organization grows — alignment on standards, coordination, and shared ownership.
Bring a clear point of view to Product leadership on what Product should bring to the table for engineering teams to work effectively — and expect the same in return.

Leadership Development & Organizational Health
Manage, coach, and develop the squad leads — your direct reports and the primary lever for everything else.
Build a consistent management practice across squads: how leads run their teams, coach their people, handle performance, and grow their engineers — so an engineer's experience doesn't depend on which squad they're on.
Maintain an accurate talent picture across the organization through the leads: who is growing, who needs support, who is ready for more complex work, and whether people are progressing at the pace we'd expect.
Own engineering throughput at the organizational level: how stories move through development, where they get stuck, and what to change. Find bottlenecks and work with leads to fix them.
Plan capacity and hiring ahead of need as the team scales, so process and staffing don't become the reasons delivery slows down.

Thought Partnership
Come to the table with thinking not just on how tasks get completed, but on how we organize and enable teams to complete them. Removing what's in the teams' way matters more than doing the work yourself.
Be a genuine peer to Product and business leadership — someone who strengthens strategic conversations rather than just executing their outcomes.

What Success Looks Like

First 90 days:
A clear diagnosis of current delivery bottlenecks with a recommended plan, and established expectations with leads on how teams run.
First year:
Release and development processes that scale to 21+ engineers; throughput measurably improved; a lead layer that is managing well and consistently; a talent picture leadership trusts; engineering fully represented in next-year planning.
Ongoing:
Product and engineering leadership operating like sections of the same orchestra — aligned on expectations in both directions, planning the future together.

Responsibilities and Benefits

What We're Looking For

Experience leading engineering organizations of 15–40 people through a growth phase, ideally with multiple squads in a shared codebase.
Experience managing through a leadership layer — developing leads rather than managing every engineer directly.
A track record of building right-sized process — enough structure to scale, not so much that squads lose independence.
Strong people-management instincts: coaching, performance development, and the judgment to make talent recommendations backed by direct inspection.
Fluency with delivery metrics and workflow data; comfort diagnosing bottlenecks and acting on them.
Strategic range: able to contribute to multi-year product and organizational planning, not just current-quarter execution.
A collaborative operating style with Product — a peer partner, not a service provider.

How You're Supported
As part of the Mission Pet Health family, you get the stability of a local practice backed by the comprehensive benefits and resources of a larger network. The focus is on investing in you, so you can focus on what you love.

Note: Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to support you at every stage. Eligibility for specific benefits varies based on your role and hours worked.
Competitive Compensation

A competitive hourly rate or salary based on your experience and role.
Health & Wellbeing

We offer comprehensive coverage options including Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance, along with access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for all teammates.
Financial Security

Plan for your future with our 401k retirement options and additional financial protection benefits like Life Insurance and Disability coverage.
Commitment to Growth

We support your career goals with opportunities for professional development, including educational assistance for qualified teammates to enroll in AVMA-accredited veterinary technician programs.
The Power of a Network

Join a nationwide community of over 20,000 veterinary professionals who share a passion for collaboration, career growth, and sharing best practices.
Valuable Perks

Enjoy discounted veterinary care for your own pets, access to an online discount platform, and free 24/7 access to doctors through Teladoc.

jobs.title: Hiring Event - Chief Software Engineer V
jobs.description:
Overview

Great minds meet great challenges.

Ready to build what’s next?

At PNNL, our core capabilities are divided among major departments that we refer to as Directorates within the Lab, focused on a specific area of scientific research or other function, with its own leadership team and dedicated budget.

Our Science & Technology directorates include National Security, Integrated Discovery Sciences, and Energy and Environment. In addition, we have an Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, a Department of Energy, Office of Science user facility housed on the PNNL campus.

The National Security Directorate (NSD) drives science-based, mission-focused solutions to take on complex, real-world threats to our nation and the world.

The AI and Data Analytics Division, part of NSD, combines profound domain expertise and creative integration of advanced hardware and software to deliver computational solutions that address complex data and analytic challenges. Working in multidisciplinary teams, we connect foundational research to engineering to operations, providing the tools to innovate quickly and field results faster. Our strengths are integrated across the data analytics lifecycle, from data acquisition and management to analysis and decision support.

Event Details

Our hiring event will take place during the weeks of October 12th to November 13th.

Selected candidates may be invited to participate in virtual and onsite interviews during this timeframe and will be contacted directly with scheduling details.

This role is performed full-time onsite at the PNNL campus in Richland, WA or Seattle, WA.

Responsibilities

With new projects and expanding programs, our AI and Data Analytics Division offers opportunities to advance cutting-edge research and build solutions for critical national security missions. Join a team of more than 400 data scientists, software engineers, mathematicians, and human-centered computing researchers turning ambitious ideas into real-world capabilities.

We're hiring across three complementary chief engineering tracks
, and we're looking for people who want to own something meaningful end-to-end: from the platform beneath it, to the systems that power it, to the experience humans actually touch.

Skills We’re Seeking

DevSecOps and Platform Engineering: Design and build scalable AI platforms, cloud-native infrastructure, containerized environments (Docker/Kubernetes), CI/CD pipelines, IaC, real-time data stream architectures, and reliable, secure production systems. We are particularly interested in engineers with strong Python expertise and significant experience in DevOps, platform engineering, site reliability engineering, distributed systems, telemetry and observability, security, and automated software delivery.
AI Systems & Data Platform Software Engineers: Push the boundaries of agentic AI systems characterized by autonomy, adaptability, reasoning, collaboration, and effective tool use. We are seeking experienced software engineers and nationally recognized technical leaders who have designed and deployed agentic AI systems and large-scale data platforms in real-world environments. Relevant expertise includes large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, multi-step reasoning, autonomous decision workflows, model and data orchestration, production-quality AI systems, and designing and operating petabyte-scale ETL/ELT pipelines. Senior candidates may also shape research directions, lead multidisciplinary R&D programs, develop external partnerships, and mentor AI scientists and engineers.

Learn more about the PNNL AI and Data Analytics Division.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

PhD and 5 years of relevant experience -OR-
MS/MA and 7 years of relevant experience -OR-
BS/BA and 9 years of relevant experience -OR-
AA and 18 years of relevant experience -OR-
HS/GED and 20 years of relevant experience.
Relevant experience is defined as Software Engineering experience in designing, architecting, programming, deploying, and automating software solutions in support of scientific research or consumer digital product development.

Current, hands-on software development experience using Python.

Hazardous Working Conditions/Environment

Not applicable.

Additional Information

This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a federal security clearance.

A security clearance background investigation includes review of your employment, education, financial, and criminal history, as well as interviews with you and your personal references, neighbors, and co-workers to determine trustworthiness, reliability, and loyalty to the United States. The investigation also examines your foreign connections, drug and alcohol use, foreign influence, and overall conduct.

Requirements

U.S. Citizenship
Background Investigation: Applicants selected will be subject to a Federal background investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified matter in accordance with 10 CFR 710, Appendix B.
Drug Testing: All Security Clearance positions are Testing Designated Positions, which means that the applicant selected for hire is subject to pre-employment drug testing, and post-employment random drug testing. In addition, applicants must be able to demonstrate non-use of illegal drugs, including marijuana, for the 12 consecutive months preceding completion of the requisite Questionnaire for National Security Positions (QNSP).

Note: Applicants will be considered ineligible for security clearance processing by the U.S. Department of Energy if non-use of illegal drugs, including marijuana, for 12 months cannot be demonstrated.

“Referral Eligible”

Testing Designated Position

This position is a Testing Designated Position (TDP). The candidate selected for this position will be subject to pre-employment and random drug testing for illegal drugs, including marijuana, consistent with the Controlled Substances Act and the PNNL Workplace Substance Abuse Program.

About PNNL

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is a world-class research institution powered by a highly educated, diverse workforce committed to the values of Integrity, Creativity, Collaboration, Impact, and Courage. Every year, scores of dynamic, driven people come to PNNL to work with renowned researchers on meaningful science, innovations and outcomes for the U.S. Department of Energy and other sponsors; here is your chance to be one of them!

At PNNL, you will find an exciting research environment and excellent benefits including health insurance, and flexible work schedules. PNNL is located in eastern Washington State—the dry side of Washington known for its stellar outdoor recreation and affordable cost of living. The Lab’s campus is only a 45-minute flight (or ~3 hour drive) from Seattle or Portland, and is serviced by the convenient PSC airport, connected to 8 major hubs.

Commitment to Excellence and Equal Employment Opportunity

Our laboratory is committed to fostering a work environment where all individuals are treated with fairness and respect while solving critical challenges in fundamental sciences, national security, and energy resiliency. We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is an Equal Opportunity Employer. PNNL considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information (including family medical history), protected veteran status, and any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local laws.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures and in employment. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, contact us at careers@pnnl.gov.

Drug Free Workplace

PNNL is committed to a drug-free workplace supported by Workplace Substance Abuse Program (WSAP) and complies with federal laws prohibiting the possession and use of illegal drugs.

If you are offered employment at PNNL, you must pass a drug test prior to commencing employment. PNNL complies with federal law regarding illegal drug use. Under federal law, marijuana remains an illegal drug. If you test positive for any illegal controlled substance, including marijuana, your offer of employment will be withdrawn.

Security, Credentialing, And Eligibility Requirements

As a national laboratory, PNNL is responsible for adhering to the Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) and Department of Energy (DOE) Order 473.1A, which require new employees to obtain and maintain a HSPD-12 Personal Identify Verification (PIV) Credential. To obtain this credential, new employees must successfully complete the applicable tier of federal background investigation post hire and receive a favorable federal adjudication. The tier of federal background investigation will be determined by job duties and national security or public trust responsibilities associated with the job. All tiers of investigation include a declaration of illegal drug activities, including use, supply, possession, or manufacture within the last 1 to 7 years (depending on the applicable tier of investigation). Illegal drug activities include marijuana and cannabis derivatives, which are still considered illegal under federal law, regardless of state laws.

For Foreign National Candidates

If you have not resided in the U.S. for three consecutive years, you are not eligible for the PIV credential and instead will need to obtain a favorable Local Site Specific Only (LSSO) Federal risk determination to maintain employment. Once you meet the three-year residency requirement thereafter, you will be required to obtain a PIV credential to maintain employment. jobs.description:
Overview

Great minds meet great challenges.

Ready to build what’s next?

At PNNL, our core capabilities are divided among major departments that we refer to as Directorates within the Lab, focused on a specific area of scientific research or other function, with its own leadership team and dedicated budget.

Our Science & Technology directorates include National Security, Integrated Discovery Sciences, and Energy and Environment. In addition, we have an Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, a Department of Energy, Office of Science user facility housed on the PNNL campus.

The National Security Directorate (NSD) drives science-based, mission-focused solutions to take on complex, real-world threats to our nation and the world.

The AI and Data Analytics Division, part of NSD, combines profound domain expertise and creative integration of advanced hardware and software to deliver computational solutions that address complex data and analytic challenges. Working in multidisciplinary teams, we connect foundational research to engineering to operations, providing the tools to innovate quickly and field results faster. Our strengths are integrated across the data analytics lifecycle, from data acquisition and management to analysis and decision support.

Event Details

Our hiring event will take place during the weeks of October 12th to November 13th.

Selected candidates may be invited to participate in virtual and onsite interviews during this timeframe and will be contacted directly with scheduling details.

This role is performed full-time onsite at the PNNL campus in Richland, WA or Seattle, WA.

Responsibilities

With new projects and expanding programs, our AI and Data Analytics Division offers opportunities to advance cutting-edge research and build solutions for critical national security missions. Join a team of more than 400 data scientists, software engineers, mathematicians, and human-centered computing researchers turning ambitious ideas into real-world capabilities.

We're hiring across three complementary chief engineering tracks
, and we're looking for people who want to own something meaningful end-to-end: from the platform beneath it, to the systems that power it, to the experience humans actually touch.

Skills We’re Seeking

DevSecOps and Platform Engineering: Design and build scalable AI platforms, cloud-native infrastructure, containerized environments (Docker/Kubernetes), CI/CD pipelines, IaC, real-time data stream architectures, and reliable, secure production systems. We are particularly interested in engineers with strong Python expertise and significant experience in DevOps, platform engineering, site reliability engineering, distributed systems, telemetry and observability, security, and automated software delivery.
AI Systems & Data Platform Software Engineers: Push the boundaries of agentic AI systems characterized by autonomy, adaptability, reasoning, collaboration, and effective tool use. We are seeking experienced software engineers and nationally recognized technical leaders who have designed and deployed agentic AI systems and large-scale data platforms in real-world environments. Relevant expertise includes large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, multi-step reasoning, autonomous decision workflows, model and data orchestration, production-quality AI systems, and designing and operating petabyte-scale ETL/ELT pipelines. Senior candidates may also shape research directions, lead multidisciplinary R&D programs, develop external partnerships, and mentor AI scientists and engineers.

Learn more about the PNNL AI and Data Analytics Division.

Qualifications

PhD and 5 years of relevant experience -OR-
MS/MA and 7 years of relevant experience -OR-
BS/BA and 9 years of relevant experience -OR-
AA and 18 years of relevant experience -OR-
HS/GED and 20 years of relevant experience.
Relevant experience is defined as Software Engineering experience in designing, architecting, programming, deploying, and automating software solutions in support of scientific research or consumer digital product development.

Current, hands-on software development experience using Python.

Additional Information

This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a federal security clearance.

A security clearance background investigation includes review of your employment, education, financial, and criminal history, as well as interviews with you and your personal references, neighbors, and co-workers to determine trustworthiness, reliability, and loyalty to the United States. The investigation also examines your foreign connections, drug and alcohol use, foreign influence, and overall conduct.

U.S. Citizenship

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is a world-class research institution powered by a highly educated, diverse workforce committed to the values of Integrity, Creativity, Collaboration, Impact, and Courage. Profluent is the frontier AI lab for biology. Profluent builds powerful foundation models for all of life's molecules, unlocking solutions that transform medicine, agriculture, and beyond. Define the software and data architecture, system boundaries, and data flows connecting computational design, high-throughput experimentation, analysis, and machine learning
Architect and guide delivery of scientist-facing applications and data systems supporting experimental design, sample tracking, laboratory automation, assay data capture, and analysis
Establish scalable data models and standards for identifiers, provenance, lineage, versioning, interoperability, and access control, ensuring experimental results are reliable, reusable, and model-ready
Partner across science, automation, bioinformatics, data science, and ML while establishing strong engineering and product practices that drive reliable delivery and adoption

Track record of leading teams that architect and deliver production-quality, data-intensive software platforms
Strong technical foundation in Python, backend systems, databases, APIs, cloud infrastructure, and modern software development practices
Experience designing data architectures, schemas, and domain models for complex scientific, experimental, or similarly interconnected workflows
Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous user and scientific needs into reliable systems, make sound technical and product tradeoffs, and drive adoption

Experience building scientific data infrastructure, research software, LIMS integrations, or scientist-facing applications
Experience with Benchling, laboratory automation, instrument integration, sample tracking, or high-throughput experimental platforms

Frontend development experience and an interest in building intuitive scientist-facing interfaces

High-growth opportunity with meaningful impact on the future of protein design
Competitive compensation package with equity participation

Description

About the Role

Virtium is seeking a Senior VP, Technology to help define the next chapter of our technology strategy as we expand from our strong foundation in industrial memory and storage into broader embedded computing, Edge AI, connectivity, and integrated system-level solutions.

This is a highly visible executive role for a senior technology leader who can combine deep technical credibility, customer insight, product vision, and practical business judgment. The Senior VP, Technology will partner directly with the CTO, executive leadership, customers, technology partners, and internal teams to shape where Virtium invests, differentiates, and grows.

About Virtium

Virtium is a Rancho Santa Margarita, California–based designer and manufacturer of high-reliability industrial embedded solutions for customers whose systems must operate consistently in demanding, long-life environments. For more than 25 years, Virtium has supported global OEMs with industrial-grade SSDs, DRAM memory modules, compute and system-on-module solutions, AI accelerator modules, connectivity modules, and supporting software.

Our solutions are used in applications across networking and telecommunications, industrial automation, aerospace and defense, medical, transportation, rugged computing, Industrial IoT, and other mission-critical embedded markets where reliability, lifecycle stability, qualification, and supply continuity matter.

Why This Role Matters

Virtium’s customers are navigating increasing complexity across embedded computing, Edge AI workloads, memory and storage requirements, semiconductor transitions, security expectations, and long product lifecycles. The Senior VP, Technology will help identify where customer requirements, emerging technologies, supplier roadmaps, and market opportunities intersect—and translate those insights into differentiated solutions, strategic partnerships, and scalable product opportunities.

The right leader will have the chance to influence Virtium’s technology direction at a meaningful stage of growth, with direct access to executive decision-making and a clear connection between strategy, customer need, product development, and market impact.

What You’ll Lead

Reporting to the CTO, the Senior VP, Technology will serve as Virtium’s senior technology strategist and trusted technical voice with customers, suppliers, partners, and internal teams. This leader will guide through technical credibility, strategic judgment, collaboration, and cross-functional influence while partnering closely with engineering leadership responsible for development execution.

Key Areas of Impact

Customer and Market Strategy: Build trusted-advisor relationships with strategic OEM customers, understand their embedded system architecture and future requirements, and identify where Virtium can create differentiated technical and commercial value.
Technology and Product Roadmap: Define and maintain Virtium’s long-term roadmap across industrial SSDs, DRAM memory, compute/SOM platforms, AI accelerator modules, connectivity modules, and related software-enabled solutions.
Technology Ecosystem Leadership: Develop strategic relationships with semiconductor manufacturers, processor and controller suppliers, memory and NAND partners, AI accelerator providers, connectivity partners, and other key technology ecosystem partners.
Architecture and Technical Direction: Guide major platform, architecture, and technology decisions across hardware, firmware, software, edge workload performance, system integration, thermal and power constraints, reliability, qualification, validation, and lifecycle requirements.
Executive Alignment and Growth: Align executive, commercial, product, engineering, operations, and supply chain teams around focused technology priorities that support customer value, differentiation, revenue growth, manufacturability, and time to market.

Ideal Candidate Profile

Executive-level technology leader with 15+ years of relevant experience in embedded systems, edge computing, memory, storage, semiconductors, computing hardware, connectivity, industrial hardware, or complex hardware/software platforms.
Strong customer-facing Senior VP, Technology, VP Engineering, Chief Architect, Distinguished Engineer, Fellow, or senior technology leadership background with credibility across OEM customers, engineering teams, suppliers, and executive stakeholders.
Deep understanding of how to balance innovation with reliability, lifecycle stability, manufacturability, qualification, security, performance, and supply continuity in demanding embedded or mission-critical environments.
Proven ability to translate customer and market insight into technology roadmaps, scalable product opportunities, strategic partnerships, and practical execution priorities.
Comfortable operating in a hands-on, collaborative, growth-oriented environment where influence, clarity, judgment, and customer proximity matter.
Bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related technical discipline

Location and Logistics

new_jobs.description:
Overview

Great Day Improvements - Senior Director, Infrastructure & Operations

Job-type:
Full-Time, exempt.

Location:
On-site role based out of Twinsburg, OH; Cincinnati, OH; or Somerset, NJ. Candidates must currently live within a commutable distance of one of these locations or be willing to relocate.

Salary Range:
$160,000 – $180,000 base compensation. This range represents a good faith estimate of the expected base salary for this position. Final base salary will be determined based on factors including, but not limited to, the candidate’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, and alignment with market data.

Job Summary

The Senior Director, Infrastructure & Operations is responsible for leading the teams that support the company’s enterprise technology foundation, including infrastructure, network, cloud, data center, identity and access management, endpoint computing, collaboration platforms, service desk operations, and infrastructure security and risk support.

This role supports a national, highly distributed environment across branch locations, manufacturing facilities, corporate offices, and data centers. The Senior Director will ensure critical technology services remain stable, secure, scalable, resilient, and aligned with business needs.

The ideal candidate is an experienced infrastructure and operations leader who began their career in a hands-on technical role and progressed into senior leadership. This individual will partner closely with executives and technical teams, assess current operations, build practical roadmaps, improve service levels, develop talent, strengthen accountability, and drive continuous improvement across the organization.

Application development, ERP systems, enterprise integrations, business intelligence, and software engineering are managed by a separate technology organization and are not part of this role.

Responsibilities

Infrastructure & Operations Leadership

Set the strategic direction for enterprise infrastructure and operations, developing roadmaps that support business growth, scalability, security, and evolving business needs while evaluating current platforms, identifying gaps, prioritizing improvements, and establishing consistent operational standards, processes, and expectations.
Serve as a trusted advisor to executive leadership on infrastructure decisions, investments, and risks, partnering with enterprise technology leadership to ensure infrastructure, identity, and endpoint platforms are prepared to support AI tools and services across the organization.
Participate in enterprise AI governance, evaluating the infrastructure, security, and data implications of new AI tools and technologies entering the environment.

IT Operations

Lead day-to-day enterprise infrastructure and support operations, creating consistency in incident, change, problem, and outage management while improving service quality, responsiveness, and the overall user experience.
Strengthen operational visibility through monitoring, reporting, and performance metrics, and partner with business leaders to understand challenges, remove technology obstacles, and improve service delivery.

Network, Cloud & Infrastructure Services

Oversee enterprise networking and telecommunications, including WAN, SD-WAN, LAN, wireless, internet connectivity, and related services, while leading hybrid cloud and on-premise infrastructure environments.
Lead infrastructure modernization through automation and platform improvements, while managing data center operations, backup platforms, recovery capabilities, infrastructure lifecycle planning, and initiatives designed to reduce operational risk through sound architecture, planning, and execution.

Identity, Security & Risk

Partner closely with cybersecurity leadership on infrastructure security initiatives, including identity and access management, vulnerability remediation, security incident response and recovery, compliance with internal security standards, and audit requirements.
Support the secure deployment and adoption of AI platforms by enforcing identity, access, and data protection standards across AI-enabled applications and services and assessing risks related to data handling, endpoint controls, and acceptable-use enforcement.

Operational Metrics & Performance Management

Establish and maintain Infrastructure and Service Desk KPIs, operational scorecards, and executive dashboards that provide visibility into infrastructure health, service performance, operational risk, customer satisfaction, and team productivity.
Track and report key metrics including infrastructure availability, SLA attainment, MTTR, MTTD, First Contact Resolution, change success rates, incident trends, vulnerability remediation, endpoint compliance, and customer satisfaction.
Present operational performance, trends, risks, and improvement plans to executive leadership, using data and measurable outcomes to identify improvement opportunities, strengthen accountability, and drive decisions based on business impact.

Team Leadership

Lead, coach, develop, recruit, and retain a strong team of infrastructure and operations professionals, establishing clear priorities, expectations, and accountability while building future leaders.
Foster a culture of ownership, open communication, follow-through, and accountability across the organization.

Business Partnership & Vendor Management

Build strong relationships with executives, business leaders, and operational stakeholders, translating technical concepts into clear business terms and partnering effectively across the organization.
Manage technology vendors, service providers, and strategic partners while overseeing infrastructure budgets, technology-related operating expenses, contracts, and investments to maximize value and reduce risk.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field strongly preferred; equivalent relevant experience may also be considered.
12+ years of progressive experience in infrastructure and operations environments, including at least 5 years leading infrastructure, network, cloud, platform, or IT operations teams.
Prior experience reporting directly to a CIO, CTO, Executive Vice President, Senior Vice President, or equivalent executive technology leader.
Previous hands-on technical experience as a Systems Administrator, Infrastructure Engineer, Network Engineer, Cloud Engineer, Architect, or similar role.
Experience supporting organizations with at least 2,500 employees across multiple locations.
Experience leading hybrid cloud and on-premise infrastructure environments, with strong knowledge of enterprise networking, cloud services, identity management, endpoint management, and infrastructure operations.
Experience leading Service Desk and end-user support organizations.
Experience managing technology vendors, service providers, contracts, budgets, and related operating expenses.
Experience developing and managing Infrastructure and Service Desk KPIs, operational scorecards, and executive dashboards.
Demonstrated experience presenting operational performance, risks, trends, and improvement plans to executive leadership.
Experience leading infrastructure and operations teams through growth, organizational change, acquisitions, transformation, or similar periods of significant change.
Strong communication skills and executive presence.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in a related field.
Experience supporting highly distributed organizations, including manufacturing, distribution, retail, field services, or similar environments.
Experience supporting organizations with 3,000+ employees and 100+ locations.
Experience leading infrastructure modernization initiatives.
Infrastructure architecture or enterprise architecture experience.
ITIL certification or experience working within a similar operational framework.
Relevant professional certifications such as CISSP, CCNP, Azure, AWS, VMware, PMP, or ITIL.
Working knowledge of AI platform infrastructure requirements, including data security, licensing, and endpoint considerations.

The Technical Executive Director, SAP Basis & Platform Operations, is responsible for ensuring the stability, security, and performance of the current global SAP environment.

Partnering with Enterprise Architecture, SAP functional/engineering leadership, and infrastructure teams, this position will define and execute a multi-year transformation roadmap, aligning SAP platform capabilities with long-term business strategy. Success in this role requires the ability to lead through change, operate within shared responsibility models (RISE), and balance current-state reliability with future-state innovation.

Partner with enterprise architecture and SAP leadership to drive innovation and future-state platform capabilities

Coordinate effectively within SAP-managed and hybrid cloud service models

Risk, Security & Compliance

Oversee vulnerability management, patching strategies, and risk mitigation efforts
Ensure readiness for disaster recovery and business continuity scenarios

Leadership & Talent Development

Mentor and develop talent aligned to modern SAP and cloud capabilities

10+ years of experience in SAP Basis, platform engineering, or SAP technical operations within large-scale, global environments
5+ years of leadership experience managing SAP Basis teams and/or managed service providers
Proven track record of leading SAP platform transformation initiatives, including modernization and cloud adoption
Experience operating in complex, highly integrated SAP landscapes, preferably supporting a single global instance or similarly scaled environment

new_jobs.title: Director, Software Technical Product Management
new_jobs.description:
What if the work you did every day could impact the lives of people you know? Or all of humanity?

At Illumina, we are expanding access to genomic technology to realize health equity for billions of people around the world. Our efforts enable life-changing discoveries that are transforming human health through the early detection and diagnosis of diseases and new treatment options for patients.

Working at Illumina means being part of something bigger than yourself. Every person, in every role, has the opportunity to make a difference. Surrounded by extraordinary people, inspiring leaders, and world changing projects, you will do more and become more than you ever thought possible.

Position Summary

Illumina's BioInsight Platform Core is the software foundation on which customers connect instruments, manage samples and projects, store and move data, run analysis workflows, and explore results — across cloud and on-prem deployments. As Director of Software Technical Product Management, BioInsight Platform Core Product, you own the product strategy, roadmap, and delivery partnership for Platform Core: the application-facing capabilities historically delivered as Illumina Connected Analytics (ICA) and related platform surfaces.

You own instrument connectivity, data storage and data movement, workflow / pipeline execution, sample and project management, notebooks and interactive analysis, platform user experience, and APIs / developer experience — the product capabilities that make BioInsight Platform the durable home for Illumina software applications. You partner tightly with other software product leaders, as well as stakeholders across Engineering, Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Finance, and Legal.

Scope of Responsibilities

Own BioInsight Platform Core product end-to-end: vision, multi-release roadmap, requirements quality, and release readiness for core platform capabilities
Lead a team of software technical product managers; hire, coach, and set the bar for platform product excellence
Serve as the primary product partner to platform engineering leadership on architecture bets, technical debt, reliability, performance, and security of core capabilities
Define outcome metrics for platform success: availability, time-to-first-analysis, workflow success rate, storage and data-movement reliability, notebook / interactive-analysis adoption, API adoption, and support burden
Ensure Platform Core meets enterprise and regulated-customer expectations for the capabilities it owns (security, privacy, auditability, quality-system interfaces where applicable)
Navigate ambiguity across a platform that serves many applications; create a coherent product narrative and prioritization framework
Represent BioInsight Platform Core in BioInsight leadership forums; escalate tradeoffs with clear recommendations

Responsibilities

Establish a multi-year roadmap for BioInsight Platform Core with clear problem statements and success metrics
Own product requirements for core platform capabilities, including: Instrument connectivity — sequencer and lab instrument connection, run data ingress, status, and operational reliability Data storage and data movement — customer data stores, import/export, retention/lifecycle behaviors that affect product experience (commercial storage packaging partners with Commercialization) Workflow and pipeline execution — defining, launching, monitoring, and operating analysis workflows at scale Sample and project management — organizing biological and analysis context that applications and workflows depend on Notebooks and interactive analysis — exploratory / interactive compute experiences on platform data Platform UX and APIs — console experience, developer surfaces, and integration contracts used by applications and customers
Partner with engineering leaders and architects to land technical bets safely; manage quality, cost, performance, and time tradeoffs
Lead customer and field discovery on core-product friction (instrument connection, storage/workflow failures, notebook UX, API gaps, cross-application platform gaps); synthesize into prioritized bets
Align with application TPMs (DRAGEN, Oncology / ICI, Genetic Disease, Multiomics, Orchestration) so Platform Core investments unlock portfolio-level outcomes
Partner with the Commercialization Director at the boundary where core capabilities meet commercial systems (e.g., storage tiers that are sold, workflow compute that is metered) — Commercialization owns tenancy, IAM, entitlements, usage metering, and billing; Core owns the product capability customers use
Define and review launch and post-market quality plans for Platform Core releases; engage Quality/Security/Privacy as needed
Instrument core capabilities for product telemetry; drive iteration loops that improve adoption and reduce support load
Support strategic customer engagements where Platform Core architecture, roadmap, or reliability is decisive
Build and develop the core product team; raise the bar on PRDs, documentation, and cross-functional working agreements

Listed responsibilities are an essential, but not exhaustive list, of the usual duties associated with the position. Changes to individual responsibilities may occur due to business needs.

Experience / Education

Typically requires a Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 18 years of related experience in a technical field (computer science, bioinformatics, engineering, life sciences, or related) or equivalent experience; advanced degree a plus
Typically 12+ years of progressive experience in product management for scientific, data, or analysis platforms (workflow/pipeline systems, data platforms, instrument-to-cloud software, or developer-facing platforms), with 5+ years leading managers or senior ICs
Track record shipping platform capabilities at scale — e.g., storage/data services, workflow orchestration or pipeline execution, notebooks / interactive compute, instrument or device connectivity, or APIs used by multiple consuming applications
Experience in life sciences, health tech, genomics, or regulated software strongly preferred; prior ICA, BaseSpace, or equivalent genomics-platform experience is a significant plus
Comfortable discussing architecture, APIs, data models, SLAs, and security with engineering leaders
Strong executive communication skills; ability to create clarity under ambiguity
Familiarity with AWS, Azure, or GCP and with hybrid / on-prem deployment models is a plus

Requirements

Proven ability to craft platform strategy, translate it into roadmaps, and ship iteratively
Experience collaborating with engineering, design/UX, security, quality, and commercial teams
Working knowledge of the software development lifecycle; design controls / ISO 13485 experience a plus where platform touches regulated workflows
Ability to balance the needs of many consuming products without becoming a pure intake function
Experience building or scaling a product management team; mentoring senior PMs
Analytical rigor: product telemetry, reliability and workflow success metrics, adoption funnels, prioritization frameworks

All listed requirements are deemed as essential functions to this position; however, business conditions may require reasonable accommodations for additional task and responsibilities.

new_jobs.title: Technical Director, PLM Platform Engineering
new_jobs.description:
The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.
is one of the world’s leading manufacturers, marketers, and sellers of quality skin care, makeup, fragrance, and hair care products, and is a steward of luxury and prestige brands globally. The company’s products are sold in approximately 150 countries and territories under brand names including: Estée Lauder, Aramis, Clinique, Lab Series, Origins, M·A·C, La Mer, Bobbi Brown Cosmetics, Aveda, Jo Malone London, Bumble and bumble, Darphin Paris, TOM FORD, Smashbox, AERIN Beauty, Le Labo, Editions de Parfums Frédéric Malle, GLAMGLOW, KILIAN PARIS, Too Faced, Dr.Jart+, the DECIEM family of brands, including The Ordinary and NIOD, and BALMAIN Beauty.

Description

The Director, Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) Platform Engineering is responsible for defining and executing the engineering strategy, platform governance, modernization, and long-term evolution of the enterprise Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) platform supporting global Research & Development, Product Development, Quality, Manufacturing, and Regulatory business capabilities.

Reporting to the Executive Director, ERP & Value Chain Platform Engineering, this role provides strategic leadership for the engineering realization, lifecycle management, and continuous improvement of the enterprise PLM platform while ensuring alignment with business priorities, enterprise architecture standards, and enterprise technology strategy. The Director partners closely with Product and Technology leaders, Enterprise Architecture, Enterprise Business Services (EBS), Operations & Infrastructure, Cyber Security, and strategic technology partners to deliver secure, scalable, and reliable PLM capabilities that enable product innovation and lifecycle management across the enterprise.

This leader will play a key role in the organization's PLM modernization strategy by providing technical leadership during enterprise platform evaluations, solution assessments, vendor demonstrations, technical proof-of-concept activities, and implementation planning supporting the selection and adoption of future-state Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) PLM solutions. The role requires practical experience with enterprise PLM implementations, modernization initiatives, and migration strategies from legacy or custom PLM environments to enterprise-grade platforms.

The Director is responsible for ensuring the PLM platform effectively supports the broader enterprise application landscape by enabling efficient collaboration across upstream product development processes and downstream enterprise capabilities, including ERP, Manufacturing, Quality, and Regulatory systems. Success in this role requires balancing strategic platform modernization with engineering excellence, operational stability, platform scalability, and long-term business value.

The ideal candidate combines deep expertise with enterprise Product Lifecycle Management platforms such as Dassault ENOVIA, Siemens Teamcenter, SAP PLM, or similar enterprise-grade solutions, along with demonstrated success leading complex PLM transformations, platform engineering organizations, and large-scale enterprise technology initiatives.

Key Roles & Responsibilities

Platform Strategy, Ownership & Lifecycle (35%)

Own the platform roadmap, lifecycle strategy, modernization initiatives, and long-term evolution of the enterprise Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) platform supporting global Research & Development, Product Development, Quality, Manufacturing, and Regulatory business capabilities.
Develop and execute platform strategies that improve scalability, engineering efficiency, business value, and long-term technology sustainability while aligning with enterprise architecture standards and organizational priorities.
Provide technical leadership for the evaluation, selection, and adoption of enterprise Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) platforms, including solution assessments, technical proof-of-concept activities, implementation planning, and migration strategy.
Develop enterprise migration strategies that enable the successful transition from legacy or custom Product Lifecycle Management solutions to modern Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) PLM platforms while minimizing business disruption and preserving critical product lifecycle information.
Lead the Enterprise Platform Engineering organization's engagement with the selected System Integrator (SI) throughout the implementation of the enterprise PLM platform, providing technical direction, engineering governance, design oversight, implementation guidance, and quality assurance while ensuring successful knowledge transfer, operational readiness, and long-term platform sustainability.
Establish enterprise engineering standards, platform roadmaps, lifecycle plans, modernization strategies, and technical governance that enable the organization to maximize the long-term value of the PLM platform.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture to ensure PLM platform capabilities align with enterprise technology standards, engineering principles, security requirements, and long-term architectural direction.

Key Roles & Responsibilities (Continued)

Platform Ownership & Delivery Governance (30%)

Provide strategic oversight for engineering realization across Enterprise Business Services (EBS), strategic technology partners, and the Enterprise Platform Engineering organization, ensuring high-quality delivery, platform stability, and operational excellence.
Establish engineering governance, release management, platform lifecycle management, environment strategy, and delivery standards supporting enterprise PLM capabilities.
Establish and mature the long-term engineering operating model for the enterprise PLM platform following implementation, including engineering governance, release management, platform lifecycle management, technical standards, enhancement delivery, and effective partnership with Enterprise Business Services (EBS).
Ensure engineering solutions are scalable, maintainable, secure, and aligned with enterprise quality standards while supporting long-term platform sustainability.
Ensure GxP-relevant PLM capabilities, implementations, and lifecycle changes adhere to established Computer System Validation (CSV), quality management, data integrity, and regulatory requirements throughout the platform lifecycle.
Govern validation readiness and execution for GxP-relevant platform implementations and changes, ensuring appropriate risk-based validation, qualification, requirements traceability, testing, documentation, deviation management, and release approval processes are completed in partnership with Quality and Validation teams.
Ensure validated PLM capabilities remain in a controlled state throughout their lifecycle, including upgrades, patches, configuration changes, integrations, releases, and environment migrations.
Drive platform optimization through continuous improvement, technical debt reduction, engineering automation, platform modernization, and operational efficiency initiatives.
Manage platform risks, engineering dependencies, technology roadmaps, software lifecycle planning, and technical decision-making to ensure long-term platform success.

Key Roles & Responsibilities (Continued)

Product Partnership & Platform Realization (20%)

Partner with Product and Technology leaders to define platform priorities, engineering roadmaps, modernization strategies, and long-term investment plans supporting enterprise Product Lifecycle Management capabilities.
Collaborate with Enterprise Architecture, Operations & Infrastructure, Cyber Security, Enterprise Business Services (EBS), business stakeholders, strategic technology partners, and the selected System Integrator (SI) to successfully deliver enterprise PLM capabilities and modernization initiatives.
Partner with Quality, Validation, Regulatory, Cyber Security, and other appropriate stakeholders to ensure GxP-relevant platform capabilities meet applicable validation, compliance, security, and data integrity requirements.
Ensure the PLM platform effectively supports enterprise business processes while enabling seamless interoperability with upstream product development processes and downstream enterprise capabilities, including ERP, Manufacturing, Quality, and Regulatory systems.
Provide engineering leadership for major platform initiatives, ensuring technical quality, delivery excellence, operational readiness, and successful business adoption.
Balance business priorities, engineering capacity, platform sustainability, and modernization objectives while driving continuous improvement across the PLM platform.

Key Roles & Responsibilities (Continued)

Engineering Leadership, Platform Excellence & Organizational Capability (15%)

Build and develop a high-performing engineering organization by mentoring engineering leaders, strengthening technical capabilities, fostering innovation, and promoting engineering excellence across the PLM platform.
Lead Enterprise Business Services (EBS), strategic technology partners, and the Enterprise Platform Engineering organization through clear engineering governance, technical leadership, delivery accountability, and organizational alignment.
Champion modern engineering practices, AI-enabled engineering capabilities, automation, reusable engineering assets, and continuous improvement to enhance engineering productivity, platform quality, and organizational effectiveness.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous learning, and engineering excellence while developing organizational capability to support the long-term success of the enterprise PLM platform.
Promote knowledge transfer, technical documentation, and engineering standards that ensure long-term platform sustainability and organizational readiness.

Qualifications

Enterprise Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) Leadership & Platform Expertise

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, Product Development, or a related technical discipline.
8+ years of progressive leadership experience governing enterprise Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) platforms, engineering applications, or enterprise technology organizations within complex global enterprises.
Demonstrated experience leading engineering organizations responsible for enterprise PLM platforms supporting Research & Development, Product Development, Manufacturing, Quality, and Regulatory business capabilities.
Deep understanding of enterprise Product Lifecycle Management processes, platform architecture, product structures, engineering change management, configuration management, and product development workflows.
Proven ability to develop long-term platform strategies that balance business priorities, technical sustainability, modernization objectives, engineering capacity, and operational excellence.
Experience supporting global Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), Manufacturing, Life Sciences, or similarly complex multinational organizations is strongly preferred.

Qualifications (Continued)

Enterprise PLM Modernization, Implementation & Engineering Leadership

Demonstrated experience leading or providing technical leadership for an end-to-end enterprise Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) implementation, including platform evaluation, solution selection, engineering realization, legacy data migration, deployment, and post-implementation operational transition, is strongly preferred.
Proven experience evaluating and implementing enterprise Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Product Lifecycle Management platforms such as Dassault ENOVIA, Siemens Teamcenter, SAP PLM, PTC Windchill, Oracle Agile PLM, or similar enterprise-grade solutions.
Experience providing technical leadership during enterprise platform evaluations, solution assessments, technical proof-of-concept activities, implementation planning, and vendor selection initiatives

new_jobs.title: Sr. Manager, IT Infrastructure & Operations (Remote)
new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Harte Hanks, we’re building a modern behavioral marketing company, marrying our data-driven understanding of human behavior with a seamless connection to the consumer. Through digital, direct, sampling, fulfillment, and customer care, we manage a full consumer experience that shortens the distance between behavior and action.

The Ask

The Senior Manager, IT Infrastructure & Operations is responsible for the reliable, secure, and cost-effective operation of corporate technology services while leading the modernization and simplification of Harte Hanks’ infrastructure environment. This role oversees infrastructure and cloud operations, networking, systems engineering, workplace technology, service delivery, and key service providers. The Senior Manager translates the enterprise technology roadmap into measurable execution, with particular emphasis on data center exit, cloud and SaaS adoption, infrastructure consolidation, operational resilience, automation, documentation, and continuous improvement.

Who You Are

You are a practical, hands-on technology leader who can operate today’s hybrid environment while deliberately reducing legacy complexity. You combine strong operational discipline with sound technical judgment, financial accountability, vendor management, and the ability to lead distributed teams through change. You know when to standardize, automate, outsource, consolidate, or retire technology, and you can balance modernization objectives with service continuity, security, compliance, and business needs. You communicate clearly with technical teams, business stakeholders, vendors, and senior leaders, and you build a culture of ownership, transparency, customer service, and continuous learning.

What You Will Be Doing

Lead and develop a distributed team responsible for infrastructure, cloud, systems, networking, workplace technology, service delivery, and operational support.
Maintain stable, secure, and resilient IT operations while driving a structured program to reduce legacy infrastructure and operational complexity.
Manage execution of the data center exit and infrastructure consolidation roadmap, including workload assessment, migration, decommissioning, dependency management, and risk mitigation.
Advance cloud-first and SaaS-first operating models where they provide measurable improvements in cost, scalability, resilience, security, and supportability.
Oversee corporate network services and connectivity, including deeper adoption and optimization of our Cato networking, while rationalizing site-based firewalls, switching, and other physical infrastructure where practical.
Own operational governance and cost management across Azure, AWS, SaaS platforms, network services, and infrastructure vendors, including budgeting, forecasting, utilization optimization, contract performance, and identification of savings opportunities.
Manage third-party vendors and support providers, ensuring responsibilities, service levels, deliverables, costs, risks, and performance expectations are clearly defined and met.
Establish effective monitoring, observability, alerting, incident response, problem management, change control, and service continuity practices across cloud and remaining on-premises environments.
Partner with information security to ensure infrastructure, identity, endpoint, network, and cloud services comply with company policies, control requirements, and recognized security practices.
Develop and maintain disaster recovery, resiliency, and business continuity capabilities appropriate to the company’s technology risk profile.
Work with senior IT leadership to convert enterprise technology strategy into prioritized, achievable initiatives with clear outcomes, owners, milestones, costs, dependencies, and risks.
Partner with business and technology stakeholders to distinguish technical support needs from training, adoption, or process support and improve routing, ownership, and the overall employee support experience.
Ensure services, projects, and modernization initiatives are delivered within agreed scope, schedule, budget, quality, and risk parameters.
Define and document standards, operational procedures, reference patterns, support models, inventories, and service ownership across the technology environment.
Establish and report meaningful SLAs, OLAs, KPIs, operational risks, and modernization progress measures.
Use Jira, Jira Service Management, Confluence, and related Atlassian capabilities to manage operational work, projects, documentation, reporting, and continuous improvement.
Promote practical use of automation, infrastructure as code, artificial intelligence, and modern operations practices to reduce manual work and improve service quality.
Support audits and compliance activities, including SOX, PCI, HIPAA, GDPR, and client control requests, as applicable.
Occasionally interact with Harte Hanks clients regarding technology operations, controls, or modernization initiatives.

Requirements

Demonstrated success leading infrastructure, cloud, IT operations, or service delivery teams through modernization and organizational change.
Bachelor’s degree in a technology-related discipline or equivalent practical experience.
8+ years of progressive IT experience, including significant responsibility for enterprise infrastructure, cloud, networking, systems, or technology operations.
3+ years managing technology professionals, preferably across distributed or globally remote teams supporting business-critical services.
Experience planning and executing data center exits, cloud migrations, infrastructure consolidation, platform modernization, or large-scale technology rationalization.
Strong working knowledge of Azure and/or AWS, enterprise networking, identity, endpoint management, compute, storage, resiliency, disaster recovery, and hybrid environments.
Experience operating and optimizing modern network and security platforms; experience with Cato or comparable SASE/SD-WAN services is strongly preferred.
Strong knowledge of IT Service Management, incident, problem, change, request, asset, and service-level management practices; ITIL experience is preferred.
Demonstrated experience with Jira, Jira Service Management, Confluence, and related Atlassian capabilities.
Experience managing technology budgets, cloud and SaaS consumption, vendors, managed services, contracts, renewals, and cost optimization.
Understanding of cybersecurity practices for endpoint security, identity and access management, network security, vulnerability management, logging, monitoring, and incident response.
Experience supporting regulated or audited environments and responding to internal, external, or client audit requests.
Working knowledge of infrastructure as code, automation, and scripting using tools such as Terraform, ARM/Bicep, PowerShell, Bash, JSON, Ansible, or comparable technologies.
Ability to develop roadmaps, business cases, standards, procedures, operating models, and meaningful operational reporting.
Strong leadership, coaching, delegation, prioritization, problem-solving, and root cause analysis skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical, operational, financial, and risk considerations to senior leaders and business stakeholders.
Calm, credible, and decisive during incidents, competing priorities, and periods of organizational change.

This is a highly visible technical leadership opportunity responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving controls engineering standards across a growing portfolio of mission-critical and data center projects.

The Senior Manager will serve as a key technical authority across Building Management Systems (BMS), Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS), SCADA, controls architecture, automation, and OT infrastructure.

This individual will partner closely with electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, commissioning, construction, IT/OT security, controls vendors, systems integrators, and external engineering partners to establish scalable controls standards and ensure reliable system performance from design through commissioning and operation.

The ideal candidate brings deep technical experience in data center or mission-critical controls, including hands-on knowledge of BMS and EPMS systems, controls programming and troubleshooting, system integration, commissioning, and technical standards development.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and own company-wide standards for BMS and EPMS systems across new data center developments.
Establish controls architecture standards covering electrical monitoring, mechanical systems, metering, alarm management, system integration, and network architecture.
Lead technical review of BMS, EPMS, SCADA, and controls designs throughout the project lifecycle.
Review and approve controls design packages, points lists, sequences of operation, network diagrams, and alarm matrices.
Partner with electrical engineering teams on metering, power monitoring, protective relay integration, and power-quality requirements.
Partner with mechanical engineering teams on controls strategies for chilled-water systems, CRAH/CRAC units, VFDs, economizers, and other critical mechanical equipment.
Provide technical oversight during construction, startup, commissioning, testing, and energization.
Support controls troubleshooting and integration issues involving devices, communications, programming, system interoperability, and field implementation.
Evaluate and select controls platforms, PLCs, RTUs, sensors, software, and systems integrators.
Support RFP development, vendor evaluation, bid review, and systems integrator selection.
Establish controls network standards related to redundancy, segmentation, cybersecurity, and IT/OT integration.
Partner with commissioning teams to ensure systems are designed and implemented for successful functional performance testing.
Develop strategies for automation, remote monitoring, alarm management, DCIM integration, analytics, and digital-twin capabilities.
Manage and develop relationships with controls vendors, consultants, integrators, engineering partners, and internal stakeholders.
Help build and mentor an internal controls engineering organization as the business continues to scale.

Qualifications

10+ years of progressive controls, automation, instrumentation, or building systems engineering experience.
Significant experience supporting data centers, mission-critical facilities, hyperscale environments, colocation facilities, or other complex critical infrastructure.
Strong experience with BMS and/or EPMS architecture and implementation.
Experience serving as a technical owner, discipline lead, engineering lead, or senior technical authority on large capital projects.
Hands-on understanding of controls programming, system integration, troubleshooting, and field implementation.
Strong knowledge of building automation, mechanical controls, electrical monitoring, metering, alarms, and system communications.
Experience working with controls systems integrators and external engineering partners.
Familiarity with SCADA and DCIM integration.
Knowledge of controls protocols such as BACnet, Modbus, OPC UA, SNMP, and IEC 61850.
Familiarity with OT cybersecurity, network segmentation, and controls-system security principles.
Experience supporting commissioning and functional performance testing of controls systems.
Ability to communicate complex technical concepts to engineers, contractors, vendors, executives, and other stakeholders.
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Controls/Instrumentation Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline preferred.

Preferred Experience

Experience establishing controls standards across multiple data center projects or facilities.
Background with a hyperscaler, colocation provider, mission-critical engineering firm, controls integrator, BMS/EPMS provider, or equipment manufacturer.
Experience with high-density or AI/HPC data-center environments.

new_jobs.title: Director of Engineering, Digital Experience
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

About the Role

Our Digital Experience engineering organization is growing from 16 to more than 21 engineers across multiple squads — including three squads working in a shared codebase — while delivering the most consequential initiatives on our roadmap. We're looking for a Director of Engineering to lead this organization through its next stage of growth: its strategy, its processes, its people, and its partnership with Product.
You'll lead through a layer of squad leads who own the day-to-day and performance of their squads (engineers and QA). Your job is to manage, coach, and develop those leads, inspect team-level outcomes, and own the health of the engineering organization as a whole.
The measure of this role is not individual output. It is whether the teams around you deliver faster, more predictably, and with fewer things in their way.
What You'll Own

Engineering Strategy
Be the engineering voice in strategic conversations about what we build and how we build it — participating from the first conversation on new initiatives, not after decisions are made.
Shape how the engineering organization is structured — squad composition, roles, and skill mix — to meet current-year objectives while planning for a multi-year horizon.
Own the point of view on our tech stack and architecture direction: whether what we have today supports where the product is going, and what needs to change before it becomes a constraint.
Partner with Product leadership as a peer when planning future years — Product brings the business perspective, you bring the engineering perspective, and together you organize the squads and the plans.

Engineering Leadership — Process and Tone
Set the process and tone for how engineering runs — the "how" (development and release processes) and the "what" (team functions and responsibilities) — without removing squad independence.
Establish and steward a release process appropriate for an organization of this size: who does what and why, checklists, rollback plans, and cross-team notification.
Define the development process end to end: how PRs move through the system, what the delivery pipeline looks like, how AI is incorporated into engineering work, and what happens when problems arise.
Be the leader engineers look to for expectations. When something isn't clear, work with the leads to make it clear.
Provide stewardship for the squads sharing a codebase as the organization grows — alignment on standards, coordination, and shared ownership.
Bring a clear point of view to Product leadership on what Product should bring to the table for engineering teams to work effectively — and expect the same in return.

Leadership Development & Organizational Health
Manage, coach, and develop the squad leads — your direct reports and the primary lever for everything else.
Build a consistent management practice across squads: how leads run their teams, coach their people, handle performance, and grow their engineers — so an engineer's experience doesn't depend on which squad they're on.
Maintain an accurate talent picture across the organization through the leads: who is growing, who needs support, who is ready for more complex work, and whether people are progressing at the pace we'd expect.
Own engineering throughput at the organizational level: how stories move through development, where they get stuck, and what to change. Find bottlenecks and work with leads to fix them.
Plan capacity and hiring ahead of need as the team scales, so process and staffing don't become the reasons delivery slows down.

Thought Partnership
Come to the table with thinking not just on how tasks get completed, but on how we organize and enable teams to complete them. Removing what's in the teams' way matters more than doing the work yourself.
Be a genuine peer to Product and business leadership — someone who strengthens strategic conversations rather than just executing their outcomes.

What Success Looks Like

First 90 days:
A clear diagnosis of current delivery bottlenecks with a recommended plan, and established expectations with leads on how teams run.
First year:
Release and development processes that scale to 21+ engineers; throughput measurably improved; a lead layer that is managing well and consistently; a talent picture leadership trusts; engineering fully represented in next-year planning.
Ongoing:
Product and engineering leadership operating like sections of the same orchestra — aligned on expectations in both directions, planning the future together.

Responsibilities and Benefits

What We're Looking For

Experience leading engineering organizations of 15–40 people through a growth phase, ideally with multiple squads in a shared codebase.
Experience managing through a leadership layer — developing leads rather than managing every engineer directly.
A track record of building right-sized process — enough structure to scale, not so much that squads lose independence.
Strong people-management instincts: coaching, performance development, and the judgment to make talent recommendations backed by direct inspection.
Fluency with delivery metrics and workflow data; comfort diagnosing bottlenecks and acting on them.
Strategic range: able to contribute to multi-year product and organizational planning, not just current-quarter execution.
A collaborative operating style with Product — a peer partner, not a service provider.

How You're Supported
As part of the Mission Pet Health family, you get the stability of a local practice backed by the comprehensive benefits and resources of a larger network. The focus is on investing in you, so you can focus on what you love.

Note: Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to support you at every stage. Eligibility for specific benefits varies based on your role and hours worked.
Competitive Compensation
